desc:
Cut the array nums at some position into a non-empty left part (a prefix) and a non-empty right part (the rest). You may then move at most one element from one part into the other part (its position inside the receiving part does not matter, only the sums do). The move must not empty the part it comes from.

Return true if some cut together with at most one such move makes the two parts have equal sums, and false otherwise. Values may be negative.

[2, 4, 1, 3]  -> true   (cut [2] | [4, 1, 3]; move 3 left: [2, 3] and [4, 1], both 5)
[1, 1, 1, 10] -> false
hints: Fix a cut and let d = leftSum - rightSum. If d = 0 you are already done. What does moving one element x do to d?

Moving x from the left part to the right part changes d by -2x; moving from right to left changes it by +2x. So you need d to be even and an element of value exactly d / 2 in the left part, or of value -d / 2 in the right part (values can be negative, so either side may help whatever the sign of d).

Sweep the cut to the right while maintaining a set of the values in the left part and a counter for the right part. At each cut check the three cases: d = 0; d even and the left part holds d/2 (with at least 2 elements on the left); d even and the right part holds -d/2 (with at least 2 elements on the right).
editorial: For a fixed cut let d = L - R. Moving an element of value x from the left to the right gives sums L - x and R + x, which are equal exactly when d = 2x. Moving from the right to the left needs -d = 2x. Hence a cut works if d = 0, or if d is even and the left part contains the value d/2, or if d is even and the right part contains the value -d/2. Because elements may be negative, both options must be tried whatever the sign of d. The side we take an element from must have at least two elements so that it stays non-empty.

Slide the cut from left to right. The prefix sum gives L and R = total - L. Keep a set with the distinct values of the left part and a Counter for the right part; moving the cut one step transfers a single element from the counter to the set. Every cut is processed in O(1), so the whole algorithm runs in O(n) time with O(n) space.
